markdown_report:
### Insights

**Starting point.** (1) SASRec already models ordered context. A small recent-history branch can test whether older interactions dilute current intent. (2) Electronics has 14.95% sampled wrong rankings and a −0.4812 lower-decile margin. Candidate competition deserves investigation, although these measurements do not establish HR@10. (3) Embedding similarity scores of 0.5392–0.5566 provide little evidence of severe collapse. Explicit embedding diversification is therefore a lower priority.

**Related work.** (1) [gSASRec](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/0939.pdf) motivates multiple uniform negatives and calibrated BCE. This offers a controlled response to weak separation before hard mining. (2) [HeteroTempRec](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ins.2025.122703) motivates combining local and global temporal pathways. A lightweight gate is a feasible initial adaptation. (3) [DTR4Rec](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10489-024-05875-3) motivates directional continuation signals. Such signals cannot establish equipment compatibility or satisfied demand.

### Framework and candidate ideas

The framework crosses **context selection**—full history, recent history, directed transitions—with **candidate discrimination**—single-negative BCE or multiple-negative calibrated BCE. This separates stale-context errors from weak ranking margins.

Scores below are Originality / Potential / User alignment / Model alignment / Difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each assessment gives a benefit (+) and limitation (−).

| Idea | Scores | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Multiple-negative gBCE | 3/7/4/9/3 | + Established, promising, directly targets margins, simple; − incremental, compute cost, limited intent correction, uncertain transfer. |
| Recent-window gate | 4/7/8/5/4 | + Compact temporal adaptation, reusable, targets stale interests; − familiar, may discard enduring preferences, indirect margin benefit, causal masking required. |
| Directed-transition residual | 5/7/7/6/5 | + Adds continuation evidence, reusable graph, targets unsupported adjacency; − established precedent, sparse edges, no compatibility guarantees, extra serving state. |
| **Recent-window gate with gBCE** | **4/8/8/9/5** | + Combines complementary mechanisms, practical, targets both failure types; − modest novelty, interaction uncertainty, no satisfaction labels, greater ablation cost. |

### Selected proposal

At 0% progress, select **recent-window gated SASRec with multiple-negative gBCE**, implemented in independently ablatable stages. A shared causal SASRec produces full-history and recent-window features; a small gate mixes their candidate scores. Train using the published gBCE calibration, initially with 128 uniform negatives.

This explicitly targets **older or isolated interactions treated as current demand** and **broad historical associations outranking recent specific interests**. Multiple-negative competition targets the measured weak separation, particularly in Electronics. These are hypotheses, not demonstrated improvements; compatibility and satisfied ownership remain unobserved.

Preserve all four dataset routes, seeds, splits and evaluator. Compare baseline, gate-only, gBCE-only and combined variants within the shared GPU budget; select exclusively by macro validation HR@10. Save the architecture configuration and update the predictor writer. Preserve diagnostic interfaces and measure margins using the actual mixed scores.

idea.description: Add a recent-window score pathway to per-dataset SASRec, mix it with full-history scores through a learned gate, and train with multiple uniform negatives using published gBCE.
idea.motivation: Recent-context gating addresses stale or isolated history and broad historical associations that displace specific current interests. Multiple-negative training addresses weak positive–negative separation, most pronounced in Electronics. Neither mechanism establishes compatibility, ownership satisfaction, or user dislikes.
idea.implementation_notes: Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, all four category routes, and SASREC_EPOCHS environment default 200. Write artifacts beneath the trial directory. Begin with a five-interaction recent window, a shared encoder, a scalar gate initialized toward the full-history pathway, and 128 uniform negatives. Implement gBCE from its published formulation rather than substituting ordinary averaged BCE. Exclude padding, the target, and known training-history positives from negative sampling; enforce causal encoder inputs. Compute recent-window attention causally at every training position, with positions matching prefix inference. Save gate parameters and configuration and update the predictor writer so working/predict.py reconstructs both pathways. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Expose mixed features through log2feats and compatible scoring through predict_score; use view.model directly for architecture-dependent probes. Report measured margins and their definitions; omit unavailable metadata category breakdowns. Maintain full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for the twenty diagnostic users. No training or benchmark gain is claimed here.
idea.pseudocode:
for dataset in FOUR_DATASETS:
    model = SharedSASRecWithRecentGate(config)
    for sequence, positive in training_batches:
        full = model.encode(sequence, causal=True)
        recent = model.encode(sequence, causal=True, window=5)
        gate = sigmoid(model.gate(concat(full, recent)))
        features = (1 - gate) * full + gate * recent
        negatives = sample_uniform_items(K=128, exclude=known_training_positives_and_padding_and_target)
        positive_logits = score(features, positive)
        negative_logits = score(features, negatives)
        loss = published_gBCE(positive_logits, negative_logits, calibration=0.75)
        update(loss)
    save_checkpoint_and_predictor_configuration()
compare baseline, gate_only, gBCE_only, combined using unchanged macro_validation_HR10
select checkpoint without accessing test labels

originality.positive: Combines context selection and calibrated candidate competition in a compact, testable adaptation.
originality.negative: Both components have clear precedents; the combination is incremental.

future_potential.positive: Provides a practical foundation for studying when recent context and broader preferences need different ranking supervision.
future_potential.negative: Benefits may disappear on sparse histories or categories with stable long-term preferences.

code_difficulty.positive: Shares SASRec weights and preserves dot-product inference and existing dataset routing.
code_difficulty.negative: Requires correct causal window masking, published loss calibration, predictor serialization, and matched diagnostic scoring.

related_work.title: gSASRec
contributions: Uses multiple uniform negatives and calibrated gBCE to address sampled-BCE overconfidence.
limitations: The supplied evidence does not establish gains under the four-category pinned protocol.

related_work.title: HeteroTempRec
contributions: Combines local pattern extraction, global dependencies, and personalized temporal fusion.
limitations: Motivates the temporal gate but does not validate this simplified adaptation.
Temporal relevance does not establish satisfied demand or equipment compatibility.

related_work.title: DTR4Rec
contributions: Fuses directed long-window transitions and short-window co-occurrences with sequence predictions.
limitations: Reported Amazon categories differ from the target benchmark.
Observed transitions do not identify complementarity or substitution.
